reasoning:
**Question.** The 2026 year-to-date dengue total in the latest INS Boletín Epidemiológico Semanal posted on or before 27 November 2026 (Colombia time): normally the week-46 issue (15–21 Nov), or the week-45 issue if week 46 is late. It resolves on 28 November.

**Starting point.** The week-43 issue (posted 6 Nov) gave 97,894, up 3,276 in a week, after roughly 2,770 a week over weeks 38–42. Extending about 3,000 a week for three more issues would give about 107,000.

**Recent evidence.**
- Colombian press after the week-43 issue puts the INS count at 102,164 (Diario del Sur headline, mid-November) and 102,415 "a corte del 10 de noviembre" (El Espectador, 16 Nov). That implies a week-44 increment of about 4,300–4,500, well above the earlier pace.
- El Tiempo (10 Nov), citing the week-43 bulletin: cases in weeks 39–42 (13,050) were 33.8% above weeks 35–38 (9,751); the INS describes a rising national trend, 23 of 37 territories are above expected levels, and IDEAM expects a very strong El Niño.
- Timing: recent issues appeared on the Thursday or Friday after the week ends, so the week-46 issue is due 26–27 Nov with no slack for a delay. I put about 83% on it being posted in time.

**Combining.** If week 46 resolves it, two more increments of about 3,500–5,300 each give roughly 109,000–113,000, centred near 110,900. If only week 45 is available (about 17%), the figure is near 106,500. The 16 Nov public holiday and routine reclassification of cases could trim the last increment; a continued acceleration would carry the total past 111,000.

**Forecast.** Median about 110,550; 90% interval about 106,000 to 113,150, with roughly 39% above the 111,000 upper bound and about 17% below 108,000.
question_title: What 2026 cumulative dengue case count will Colombia's INS report in the latest weekly epidemiological bulletin published on or before 27 November 2026?
